bull_bear.body:
- Self-funded ~Rs 35,000 cr/yr capex; moderate gearing; large liquid investments and strategic IOCL/GAIL holdings provide flexibility.
- Risk flag: any further **large debt-funded acquisition** could pressure capital structure and coverage metrics (and hence the rating).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Commodity / oil-price risk** — standalone revenue largely from crude; exposure to crude and gas price volatility (windfall-tax/price-control overhang as a PSU controlling domestic energy prices).
- **Reserve replacement / production decline** — high dependence on mature Mumbai High; moderate new-discovery track record; geological, technological and execution (E&P) risks.
- **Geopolitical** — OVL assets in politically unstable countries; Russia cash-repatriation constraints. (Upside: Mozambique force majeure ended Nov-2025; production expected ~2028.)
- **Project execution** — large multi-year capex implementation risk.
- **ESG / energy transition** — tightening environment/safety regulation; long-term fossil-fuel demand shift.
- **Acquisition risk** — large debt-funded M&A could weaken the credit profile.
bull_bear.title: Risks

business.body: ONGC is India's largest crude oil and natural gas company (Maharatna PSU), contributing ~63% of domestic production. Consolidated turnover ~Rs 6.63 lakh cr in FY2025; PAT Rs 37,293 cr. The group spans upstream E&P (standalone + OVL overseas), downstream refining (HPCL 54.90%, MRPL 80.94% effective / 71.63% consolidated), and petrochem (OPaL 95.69%). GoI holds 58.89% (as on 31-Dec-2025). Credit profile: domestic [ICRA]AAA (Stable) / A1+; international investment-grade (Moody's Baa3, S&P BBB, Fitch BBB-).
business.title: Snapshot

business.body:
| Metric (Rs cr unless noted) | FY2024 | FY2025 | 9M FY2026 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Operating income | 6,53,171 | 6,63,262 | 4,88,442 |
| PAT | 50,955 | 37,293 | 35,906 |
| OPBDIT/OI (EBITDA margin) | 15.67% | 13.40% | 15.92% |
| PAT/OI | 7.80% | 5.62% | 7.35% |
| Total outside liab./Tangible net worth (x) | 1.0 | 1.0 | n/a |
| Total debt/OPBDIT (x) | 1.9 | 2.1 | n/a |
| Interest coverage (x) | 7.9 | 6.1 | 7.8 |

- Profitability dipped in FY2025 (margin 13.4%, PAT down ~27% YoY) but **recovered in 9M FY2026** (margin 15.9%, interest coverage back to 7.8x).
- Liquidity **Strong**: cash & equivalents > Rs 32,000 cr as on 30-Sep-2025; investments in GoI bonds/PSUs; market value of strategic holdings in IOCL and GAIL.
- Production (oil + gas, group): **41.08 MMTOE in FY2025** (−1.68% YoY); **30.64 MMTOE in 9M FY2026** (−0.55% YoY).
- *(Stale 2022 deck context: FY22 consolidated total income Rs 5,39,200 cr, EBITDA Rs 87,311 cr, PAT Rs 49,294 cr, Debt/EBITDA 1.2x — included only to show trend, not current.)*
business.title: Financial performance (FY2024–9M FY2026, consolidated — from 2026 ICRA CR)

business.body:
- Reserves: proven reserves **~526 MMTOE as on 31-Mar-2025**.
- Concentration: top 15 producing fields ≈ 80% of production; Mumbai High key for crude, Bassein (western offshore) key for gas — high dependence on mature offshore fields that are in natural decline.
- **Daman Upside (shallow water)**: commissioning Mar–Apr 2026, peak ~5 mmscmd post-stabilisation; eligible volumes get new-framework pricing (20% premium for qualifying gas).
- **DSF-II fields**: multiple fields expected to contribute from Apr 2027.
- **KG-DWN-98/2**: under development (referenced as a cluster project; deck noted one gas field monetized) — incremental offshore volumes.
- **OALP acreage**: on track to meet Minimum Work Programme (MWP) commitments; exploration/appraisal progressing.
- OVL production broadly stable ~10 MMTOE FY2025 / ~7 MMTOE 9M FY2026.
business.title: Production profile / key projects

business.body:
- **Upstream (standalone)**: domestic crude + gas E&P; ~63% of India's production.
- **OVL (100%)**: overseas E&P — equity stakes in 30 projects across 14 countries; ~25.3% of India's oil and 15.9% of oil+gas (domestic-equivalent). Russia cash-repatriation constraints persist.
- **HPCL (54.90%)**: two refineries, total 24.5 MMTPA; large fuel-marketing/retail network.
- **MRPL (80.94% econ., 71.63% consol.)**: standalone refinery, 15 MMTPA installed capacity.
- **OPaL (95.69%)**: petrochemicals — one of the largest dual-feed crackers; JV with GAIL & GSPC.
- **ONGC Green Ltd (100%)** + OGL One (ex-PTC Energy): renewables vehicle.
- *(2022 deck list of JVs/SPVs — OTPC power 726 MW, PMHBL pipeline, IGGL NE gas grid, etc. — structure largely intact but figures stale.)*
business.title: Segment / subsidiary structure (business model)

business.body:
- Standalone revenue bulk derived from **sale of crude oil** → direct commodity-price exposure.
- Gas pricing benefits from the new framework (20% premium for qualifying new-field gas, e.g. Daman). Specific crude/gas realizations were not quantified in the 2026 CR.
business.title: Revenue mix / realizations

business.body:
- India remains heavily dependent on oil & gas imports; domestic upstream production is strategically important for energy security.
- Energy-transition / decarbonisation is a long-dated structural demand risk; for India the shift is expected to be slow-paced, so near-term credit impact is limited.
business.title: Demand / industry context

business.body:
- Dominant domestic market position with large proven reserves and a globally competitive cost structure (low F&D costs from owned drilling/work-over rig infrastructure, low manpower cost).
- Sovereign ownership (58.89% GoI) and strategic importance underpin financial flexibility and capital-market access at competitive rates.
business.title: Competitive position / moat

business.body: - GHG inventory & scope-1/scope-2 disclosures; CDM projects; renewable push via ONGC Green Ltd and collaborations. CSR leader (~Rs 500 cr/yr avg, per 2022 deck). Energy-transition flagged as long-dated, not currently credit-material.
business.title: ESG

business.body: - (No additional standalone disclosures from the alternate sources beyond the above.)
business.title: Other / notable

business.body:
- **Agency / action (19-Mar-2026, ICRA):** Long-term rating **[ICRA]AAA (Stable)** reaffirmed on the balance Rs 8,500 cr NCD programme. Reaffirmed-and-withdrawn on Rs 500 cr NCD (no amount outstanding), Rs 860 cr unplaced NCD, and Rs 25,000 cr bank facilities (at company's request). Total rated amount reduced from Rs 34,860 cr → Rs 8,500 cr.
- **Other agencies (current):** Moody's Baa3 (FC & LC, Stable); S&P BBB (Stable); Fitch BBB- (Stable); CARE AAA (Stable) NCD & CARE A1+ CP; India Ratings IND AAA (Stable) & IND A1+; commercial paper A1+ (up to Rs 10,000 cr each, CARE & India Ratings).
- **Rationale:** dominant domestic E&P position, large proven reserves (~526 MMTOE), competitive cost structure, stable subsidiary performance, strong financial position, moderate gearing, large liquid investments, sovereign ownership & strategic importance, excellent financial flexibility.
- **Leverage / coverage (consolidated):** Total debt/OPBDIT 1.9x (FY24) → 2.1x (FY25); Total outside liabilities/TNW 1.0x; Interest coverage 7.9x (FY24) → 6.1x (FY25) → 7.8x (9M FY26); TD/Equity 1.0x context.
- **Liquidity:** Strong — cash & equivalents > Rs 32,000 cr (30-Sep-2025); self-funded capex.
- **Standalone vs consolidated note:** Ratings derived on **consolidated** financials of ONGC including OVL, MRPL, HPCL, OPaL and various SPVs/JVs/associates (with ICRA adjustments for some JVs; excludes adjustment for HPCL-Mittal Energy). Capex figure of ~Rs 35,000 cr/yr is **standalone**; standalone revenue is crude-heavy.
- **Sensitivities:** Positive — not applicable (already AAA). Negative — significant deterioration in consolidated group credit metrics or weakening of GoI linkages.

outlook.body:
- Profitability expected to **remain healthy** with capex plans intact despite crude/gas volatility.
- Both oil and gas volumes estimated to **increase going forward** as new fields (Daman, DSF-II, KG-DWN-98/2) ramp up and offshore redevelopment delivers recovery gains; group intends to sustain current production levels.
- Outlook **Stable**.

drhp.business: Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited is a Government Company whose main activity is Mining & Quarrying - extraction of crude petroleum and natural gas - which accounts for 90.67% of turnover. It produces crude oil, natural gas, liquefied petroleum gas and other value-added products from onshore and offshore acreages across Indian sedimentary basins, and supplies crude oil to refineries in India. Its significant revenues are derived from sales to Oil Marketing Companies, with major customers/refiners including IOCL, BPCL, HPCL, MRPL and GAIL.

risks.note: Flagged as a key strategic risk. Prices are influenced by global demand-supply dynamics, geopolitical developments, OPEC+ production decisions and government interventions, and volatility can significantly impact revenues, profitability, cash flows, project economics and investment decisions - prolonged low prices affect investment viability while sustained high prices trigger demand-side pressures and regulatory responses. Mitigated through market monitoring, stakeholder and policymaker engagement, operational efficiency, cost optimisation, production enhancement and portfolio diversification, supported by a strong balance sheet and robust liquidity.
risks.risk: Commodity price volatility in crude oil and natural gas

risks.note: A significant share of production comes from mature and ageing assets, where natural reservoir decline, increasing water cut and infrastructure fatigue can progressively affect output levels, recovery efficiency and operating costs. Managing it requires sustained enhanced oil recovery, advanced reservoir management, production optimisation and timely redevelopment, delivered through technology-led interventions, strategic partnerships and technical collaborations.
risks.risk: Decline of mature and ageing producing assets

risks.note: Key operational risk, heightened as the Company moves into deep-water and ultra-deep-water areas with higher geological uncertainty, technical complexity and substantial capital exposure. Limited exploration success, delays in reserve conversion and natural decline from producing fields can affect future output, project economics and long-term financial performance; mitigated through an integrated technology-led exploration strategy with advanced seismic interpretation, probabilistic modelling and disciplined prospect evaluation.
risks.risk: Exploration outcome and reserve replacement risk

risks.note: Evolving decarbonisation policies, heightened stakeholder expectations and changing consumption patterns may influence the long-term outlook for fossil fuels while increasing regulatory and compliance requirements. Physical climate risks - extreme weather, cyclones, floods and rising sea levels - can impact operational infrastructure and supply chains. Response includes integrating climate into strategy and investment decisions, the Net Zero Scope 1 and 2 by 2038 commitment, methane reduction, flare minimisation, renewables expansion, carbon capture and energy efficiency.
risks.risk: Climate change and the accelerating energy transition

risks.note: Major incidents such as blowouts, fires, hydrocarbon releases, vessel collisions, natural disasters or infrastructure failures may result in injuries, environmental damage, operational disruptions and reputational impact. Managed through an HSE framework covering asset integrity, process safety, emergency preparedness and safety culture, with investment in digital monitoring, predictive maintenance, automation and risk-based inspection; the BRSR adds adherence to ISO 55000 and OISD guidelines and crisis plans for oil spills, gas leaks and fires.
risks.risk: HSE and asset integrity risk across complex offshore, onshore and processing facilities

risks.note: Inherent to the oil and gas industry - changes in pricing mechanisms, taxation regimes, royalty structures, environmental regulations and energy security policies can impact profitability, project economics and capital allocation decisions. Managed through continuous engagement with policymakers, regulators and industry stakeholders and close monitoring of regulatory developments.

Increasing digitalisation of business processes, operational technologies and critical infrastructure raises exposure to cyber threats, ransomware, data breaches and insider threats, which can affect operational continuity, data security and stakeholder confidence. India's critical oil and gas sector faced an exponential surge in coordinated cyberattacks during Operation Sindoor. Managed through a 24x7 Information Security Operations Centre handling on average more than 2.1 billion events per day, ISO 27001:2022-certified ISMS across 42 data centres, vulnerability assessments, audits, phishing drills and awareness programmes.

A key financial risk given exposure to imports, overseas operations, service contracts, equipment procurement and international investments; because oil and gas transactions are largely USD-denominated, exchange-rate movements affect both revenue and expenditure. Managed under a structured Foreign Exchange and Interest Rate Risk Management Policy, natural hedging where feasible, and periodic exposure review through a dedicated Forex Risk Management Committee.
risks.risk: Foreign exchange and interest rate volatility
